name: Watergate
hook: A break-in, a cover-up, Deep Throat and a president's resignation.

facts.label: the Watergate break-in
facts.statement: On June 17, 1972, burglars broke into the Watergate hotel and office complex in Washington, D.C.

facts.label: Richard Nixon
facts.statement: The scandal forced President Richard Nixon to resign in 1974.

facts.label: the Washington Post
facts.statement: Washington Post reporters Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein broke the story; the Post won a 1973 Pulitzer Prize for Public Service for its Watergate investigation.

facts.label: Deep Throat
facts.statement: Deep Throat, the secret source, was revealed to be former FBI official W. Mark Felt.

facts.label: Sam Ervin
facts.statement: North Carolina senator Sam Ervin chaired the Senate Watergate Committee and dismissed executive privilege as 'executive poppycock.'

facts.label: John Dean
facts.statement: John Dean, former counsel to Nixon, was the chief witness against him and wrote Blind Ambition.

facts.label: John Sirica
facts.statement: District judge John Sirica, known as 'Maximum John,' presided over the Watergate case.
